A1.justification: Both PDFs describe EvoQuality and provide readable text, equations, tables and figures supporting comparison. All 13 pages of v1 and 14 pages of v4 were inspected. v1 has no appendix; v4 adds an appendix statement about LLM assistance with manuscript editing.

before.justification: v1 reports original IQA experiments, including two evolutionary rounds, comparisons against other models, the EvoEstimate ablation and sensitivity to the number of candidate responses.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experiments and adds baseline comparisons, in-domain comparison results and multi-dataset experiments, including applying EvoQuality to VisualQuality-R1.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1, the prompts and Equations 1-6 are unchanged. Pairwise majority voting, pseudo-preferences, fidelity rewards and GRPO remain the same. Applying this procedure to a supervised VisualQuality-R1 checkpoint introduces an experimental initialization, without a documented change to the algorithm.

E1.justification: v4 additionally uses SPAQ and KADID alongside KONIQ for multi-dataset co-training (Table 4). SPAQ and KADID were already evaluation datasets in v1, so this expands training coverage while retaining the same eight IQA benchmarks and perceptual task.

E2.justification: v4 adds CONTRIQUE and Re-IQA to the corresponding NR-IQA comparison in Table 3 while retaining all previous comparators. DBCNN already appeared in v1's table; its addition to the accompanying prose and references is not a new evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: The new Table 4 evaluates multi-dataset co-training with three in-distribution datasets and five out-of-distribution datasets, and additionally tests initialization from supervised VisualQuality-R1. These are added experimental settings. The original two-round KONIQ protocol, PLCC/SRCC metrics and stated training budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v4 adds an analysis of whether self-evolution benefits an already supervised IQA model, comparing VisualQuality-R1 with VisualQuality-R1+EvoQuality in Table 4. The EvoEstimate ablation and candidate-response sensitivity analysis are unchanged; v1 Table 4 becomes v4 Table 5, and Figure 3 is retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without independent-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. The sampling of K candidate responses and the variance calculations within the reward mechanism are unchanged.

E6.justification: v4 substantially extends the results with multi-dataset comparisons, supervised-checkpoint refinement, CONTRIQUE/Re-IQA scores and a KONIQ comparison column. In the new Table 4, VisualQuality-R1+EvoQuality achieves out-of-distribution weighted PLCC/SRCC of 0.768/0.716 versus 0.722/0.666 for VisualQuality-R1. These are newly reported results, not improvements between versions under the original setting. The original result entries remain unchanged. The new Table 3 also introduces an inconsistency: Qwen2.5-VL-7B's KONIQ PLCC/SRCC are 0.703/0.761, reversed relative to Table 2's 0.761/0.703.

T1.justification: The pseudo-label definition, comparative-probability model, fidelity reward, advantage calculation, GRPO objective and KL approximation in Equations 1-6 are unchanged. Neither version contains additional theorems or proofs, including in the end matter.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion add the claim that EvoQuality can augment supervised, pre-trained IQA models to improve generalization on unseen datasets. The central self-supervised voting-and-ranking contribution and headline claims of 31.8% PLCC improvement and superiority on five of seven benchmarks remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v4 explicitly acknowledges weaker in-domain performance than supervised models and interprets the cross-dataset advantage as reduced overfitting, replacing v1's explanation involving VisualQuality-R1's all-pairs rewards. It also interprets the retained second-round results as avoiding catastrophic forgetting and discusses the additive usefulness of supervised-checkpoint refinement. Section 5 modestly expands discussion of corpus diversity and possible future perceptual applications.

D1.justification: The implementation-details passage is unchanged, retaining the pair counts, response counts, optimizer, learning rate, schedule, regularization coefficient, GPUs, batch size and epoch time. The new experiments identify their datasets and starting model but add no further implementation recipe or resource-access information.

R1.justification: v4 adds RRLRIQA and distinguishes earlier full-reference-metric pseudo-labeling from its internal-consensus approach. It also adds references for CONTRIQUE, Re-IQA, DBCNN, SSIM, VSI and AIBench. The broader related-work organization and positioning remain intact; several other reference changes merely update publication metadata for retained works.

P1.justification: v4 makes localized additions and revisions to the abstract, introduction, results and conclusion, and corrects the stray EvoRank name to EvoQuality. It adds an appendix disclosure about LLM-assisted manuscript editing. Most prose and the main section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Table 3 gains a KONIQ column and two comparator rows, and a new Table 4 displays the multi-dataset results with in-distribution and out-of-distribution groupings. The previous Table 4 becomes Table 5, while Figure 3 moves to the following page. The three figures retain their content, and the overall visual style remains stable.

improvement.justification: v4 provides useful additional comparative evidence and demonstrates that EvoQuality can improve a supervised VisualQuality-R1 checkpoint under the new multi-dataset setting. Explicit in-domain comparisons and acknowledgment of earlier pseudo-label approaches also make the paper more informative. These gains are incremental because the method and original evidence remain unchanged, and they are tempered by the newly inconsistent KONIQ PLCC/SRCC entries for Qwen2.5-VL-7B in Table 3.
